feedback_request.integration_feedback: State the base_speed used and whether line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fell from 0.95 and 1.0. Report s-bend and slalom progress against 0.147 and 0.100, and slalom steering_oscillation against 0.135. State explicitly whether the oval max_error floor (about 0.061) moved. If losses persist at the reduced speed, say so, because that would rule out curve speed as the cause.

intent: Hold the iteration 8 geometry exactly (y=0.045, ±0.055 span, 16 mm footprints, 0.12 m track, 0.035 m wheels, 0.6 kg, 0.16 x 0.12 m body) so the Integrator's base_speed change is the only variable. Hypothesis: line losses on s-bend and slalom come from curve speed, not sensing coverage. Expected: line_loss_events near 0 on s-bend and slalom, with s-bend progress at or above 0.14 and a score above 50.4.
learning: Iterations 0 to 8 show that sensing span (±0.04 to ±0.06), footprint (16 mm at every row since iteration 1), lookahead (y 0.03 to 0.06), wheel track, radius, mass and ki all leave the oval max_error floor at 0.060 to 0.063. Line losses follow the forward row (none at y=0.03 with ±0.05, about 1 per trial at y=0.045 to 0.06 with ±0.055). Forward row is the only lever that has moved bend progress. The next question is whether losses are curve-speed driven, which the Integrator's base_speed change will test.
rationale: Iteration 8 moved the forward row from y=0.06 to y=0.045 and kept the ±0.055 span. Its score was 50.36, with s-bend progress 0.147 and 0.95 line losses per trial, and slalom at 1.0 loss. Losses did not clear at the intermediate row, so the Integrator's rule applies: keep the geometry unchanged and let the controller's base_speed be the lever. Forward sensing is still the only lever that has moved bend progress (s-bend 0.040 at y=0.03, 0.146 to 0.157 at y=0.045 to 0.06). The max_error floor near 0.061 to 0.063 has not moved under any geometry change, and span, track, radius, mass and lookahead have all been tested. I considered shrinking the footprint to 0.012 m, but a smaller footprint reads less tape per sensor and could push the summed reading below the 0.05 line-loss threshold on curves, so I did not make that change now. Holding the geometry identical to iteration 8 means any change in the next race comes from the Integrator's controller change, which keeps the attribution clean. Expected result: line losses fall toward 0 on s-bend and slalom with base_speed reduced, and progress stays near 0.14 on s-bend. If losses persist at reduced speed, the geometry has no remaining sensing lever for losses and the next test is y=0.03 with ±0.055.
